_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Bound the draw so the test fails instead of hanging.**

`Stream.generate(generator::next).filter(...).limit(5)` draws until five values pass the filter. If `PathTraversalGenerator` stops emitting raw forward-slash traversals made of unreserved characters only, the filter never reaches five matches. The stream then never terminates, and the build hangs instead of reporting a failure. `AttackFamilyGuard` exists to prevent this kind of silent degradation, but this test does not use it.

Cap the number of draws and assert that five samples were collected.

```diff
             List<String> rawTraversals = Stream.generate(generator::next)
+                    .limit(2000)
                     .filter(value -> value.contains("../") && UNRESERVED_AND_SLASH.matcher(value).matches())
                     .limit(5)
                     .toList();
+            assertEquals(5, rawTraversals.size(),
+                    "PathTraversalGenerator must still emit raw unreserved-character traversals");
```
</details>

_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Bound the draw so the test fails instead of hanging.**

`Stream.generate(generator::next).filter(...).limit(5)` draws until five values pass the filter. If `PathTraversalGenerator` stops emitting raw forward-slash traversals made of unreserved characters only, the filter never reaches five matches. The stream then never terminates, and the build hangs instead of reporting a failure. `AttackFamilyGuard` exists to prevent this kind of silent degradation, but this test does not use it.

Cap the number of draws and assert that five samples were collected.

_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Do not unlink a successor's guard.**

If holder A runs past the stale threshold, holder B can reclaim its guard and enter a critical section. When A exits, this unconditional unlink removes B's guard. Holder C can then enter while B is still active, even if B and C each stay below the stale threshold. This can let concurrent `create_row` calls allocate the same sequence or pass the same slug scan. Release only the guard acquired by this invocation, and add a test in which the former holder exits after reclamation.

items.source: cuioss/OAuth-Sheriff PR review comment 4019991933 by cuioss-oliver on token-sheriff-client/src/main/java/de/cuioss/sheriff/token/client/token/RefreshTokenFamily.java
items.raw:
Not fixing — no fabricated revocation target reaches anyone who does not already hold it.

`rotatedToken` is not unverified input from a third party: `rotate(presentedToken, rotatedToken)` is documented as "the successor refresh token the AS issued", and the only caller that supplies it is the relying party itself, straight from the `RotationResult` of the exchange it just ran (see `TokenLifecycleManager.doRefresh` and the composed-caller test). The reuse path takes the successor from exactly the same argument, so the already-revoked path is no weaker. A caller that "probes" with an unrelated live token already holds that token and can revoke it directly via RFC 7009 — getting it echoed back in the classification grants no capability it did not have. Requiring a separate "post-exchange state" argument would just be a second copy of the same caller-supplied value. The javadoc on `rotate` and `RefreshTokenFamilyRevokedException` states this contract.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Creating a new `LongGenerator` instance on every call to `next()` is inefficient. It's better to create it once as a `private final` field and reuse it.

For example, you could add this field to the class:
```java
private final LongGenerator dayGenerator = new LongGenerator(-23000, 23000);
```
And then change this line to:
```java
return LocalDate.ofEpochDay(dayGenerator.next());
```
